user_query: I worked at an IT company for 5 years and 2 months. When I resigned, HR refused to pay my Gratuity, claiming 'You need 5 full years excluding notice period, and your performance was poor'.
legal_text_raw: Gratuity shall be payable to an employee on the termination of his employment after he has rendered continuous service for not less than five years... on his superannuation, retirement or resignation... Gratuity cannot be withheld for poor performance; it can only be forfeited wholly or partially for termination due to riotous/disorderly conduct or acts causing financial loss...
layman_explanation: HR is legally wrong. You only need 4 years and 240 days of continuous service to be eligible for Gratuity. Performance has absolutely nothing to do with it. Send a formal legal notice; if they deny it, complain to the Controlling Authority under the Gratuity Act. They will have to pay with interest.

user_query: I hired a freelance designer on Fiverr to make my startup's main logo. I paid him ₹10,000. Now that my startup is famous, he is demanding ₹5 Lakhs, saying he never officially assigned the 'Copyright' of the logo to me.
legal_text_raw: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the author of a work shall be the first owner of the copyright therein: Provided that... in the case of a work made in the course of the author's employment under a contract of service... the employer shall... be the first owner. (However, for freelancers/contractors, independent copyright assignment in writing is required).
layman_explanation: He is legally correct. Unlike an 'employee', a freelancer retains the copyright to their work unless you signed a specific written 'Copyright Assignment Agreement' transferring ownership to your company. Just paying him for the service is not enough. You must negotiate a buyout or redesign the logo.

user_query: I am a Hindu and my husband is Muslim. We married under the Special Marriage Act. Can his family force him to orally divorce me using 'Triple Talaq' to bypass the family courts?
legal_text_raw: Marriages solemnized under this Act can only be dissolved by a decree of divorce passed by the district court on the grounds specified in Section 27... Personal laws do not apply to marriages registered under this Act.
layman_explanation: Absolutely not. Because you registered your marriage under the secular Special Marriage Act, all religious personal laws (including Triple Talaq) are completely irrelevant and legally void. Your marriage can only be dissolved by a formal decree from an Indian civil court.

user_query: My father gave me a lot of heavy gold jewelry during my wedding (Streedhan). Now my husband and his family have locked it all in their bank locker and refuse to give me the keys, saying it belongs to 'the family'.
legal_text_raw: Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner... Includes both movable and immovable property acquired by inheritance... or at real marriage...
layman_explanation: Gifts given to you at your wedding (Streedhan) are your absolute personal property. Your husband/in-laws are merely 'trustees' of it. Refusing to return your Streedhan when demanded is a criminal breach of trust under the BNS. File an FIR immediately and claim it back.

user_query: My ex-wife has primary custody of our 8-year-old son. She has suddenly moved to a different state 1000 km away and blocked my number, completely violating my court-ordered weekend visitation rights. The local police say they can't help.
legal_text_raw: Where a guardian appointed or declared by the Court... removes the ward from the limits of its jurisdiction... the Court may, on the application of any person interested... make an order for the return of the ward... Violation of custody/visitation orders amounts to civil contempt.
layman_explanation: The police are right, this is not a criminal matter yet, it is 'Contempt of Court'. Your ex-wife has deliberately violated the family court's specific visitation order. You must urgently file a Contempt Petition in the family court that originally granted custody. The judge can fine her, order police to fetch the child, or even reverse custody to you.

user_query: A vendor gave my startup a post-dated cheque for ₹2 Lakhs. When I deposited it, it bounced. But my accountant made a mistake and only informed me about the bounce 45 days later. Now the vendor says I missed the legal deadline to sue him.
legal_text_raw: The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid...
layman_explanation: The vendor is partly correct; you missed the strict 30-day window to send a legal notice for a criminal cheque bounce case (Section 138). However, the debt is NOT dead. You can still file a civil suit for recovery of money, or re-present the cheque to the bank (if it's still within its 3-month validity period) and start the 30-day clock fresh when it bounces again.

user_query: My D2C coffee brand is called 'BrewZing'. We have a registered trademark. A huge FMCG company just launched an energy drink called 'BrewZinger' with an almost identical font and logo colors. My business will be destroyed.
legal_text_raw: A registered trade mark is infringed by a person who, not being a registered proprietor... uses in the course of trade, a mark which is identical with, or deceptively similar to, the trade mark in relation to goods or services in respect of which the trade mark is registered... likely to cause confusion on the part of the public...
layman_explanation: This is a textbook case of 'Trademark Infringement' and 'Passing Off' (creating deceptive similarity). Because your mark is registered, you have immediate legal power. Hire an IP lawyer urgently to file a suit in the High Court for an 'ex-parte injunction'. The court can order them to immediately halt all sales and recall their products.

user_query: My husband filed for divorce. I am fighting the case, but I have no income to even pay my lawyer's fees or travel to the court. My husband says it's my problem.
legal_text_raw: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings.—Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application... order the respondent to pay... the expenses of the proceeding...
layman_explanation: Your husband is wrong. Under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, if you do not have an independent income, the court will force your husband to pay for ALL your litigation expenses (lawyer fees, travel costs) AND a monthly allowance while the case is ongoing. File a Section 24 application immediately.

source_act: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 & State Shops and Establishments Act
user_query: I work in an IT company. Yesterday, the CEO suddenly called 50 of us into a room, took our laptops, and told us we are fired effective immediately because the company has 'no funds'. No notice period, no severance.
legal_text_raw: Retrenchment means the termination by the employer of the service of a workman for any reason whatsoever, otherwise than as a punishment inflicted by way of disciplinary action... No workman employed in any industry who has been in continuous service for not less than one year... shall be retrenched by that employer until the workman has been given one month's notice in writing... and the workman has been paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation...
layman_explanation: This is an illegal mass layoff ('Retrenchment'). If you have worked there for over 1 year, the company is legally mandated to give you 1 month's notice (or pay in lieu) AND retrenchment compensation (15 days pay for every year worked). You group together and file a complaint with the joint Labour Commissioner immediately.

source_act: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
user_query: I am a 70-year-old widow. I legally gifted my house to my son on the condition he would take care of me. Now he and his wife have stopped giving me food and are forcing me to live in the damp basement.
legal_text_raw: Where any senior citizen who... has transferred by way of gift or otherwise, his property, subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide the basic amenities and basic physical needs to the transferor and such transferee refuses or fails to provide such amenities and physical needs, the said transfer of property shall be deemed to have been made by fraud or coercion or under undue influence and shall at the option of the transferor be declared void by the Tribunal.
layman_explanation: You have a powerful remedy. Under the Senior Citizens Act, if a child fails to provide basic care after taking property via gift/transfer, the 'Maintenance Tribunal' (chaired by the SDM) can legally cancel the gift deed, declare it void due to fraud, and forcefully evict your son. Go directly to the local SDM office.
